_comment: What the stub model answers, one rule per page. First match wins.
Two pages from the KAFKA space on cwiki.apache.org. `document` is the ledger
key, and a Confluence page's key is its id, never its title (R1.16): a stage
is shown the key it must carry back (R3.13), so these numbers are not
decoration. `match` finds each page by its note's first line, which the
converter writes from the page's title (R8.19).
Every `span` was copied out of the NOTE, not out of the page in a browser.
The note is what the model is shown and what grounding searches (R6.4), and
the two are not the same text: task 4 finds one place they differ.
The spans keep the note's markdown -- `**JIRA**:`, the link -- because that
is what a model shown the note would quote. Grounding folds it away on both
sides (R6.20), so `JIRA: KAFKA-4514` would be found as well.
The two PNGs the ZStandard page carries have no rule here. Task 4 is where
you find out they need one, and `replies-no-document.json` is it.
If Apache edits one of these pages, its version moves, sync fetches it again,
and a span here may stop matching. Check it against the note you hold with

match: # KIP-110: Add Codec for ZStandard Compression
